recommended.rationale: Match: 30 time-loss injuries per 1000 player-match-hours, matching the Argentine senior amateur study (30.9) and CRISP England community men (29.2 in 2021-22; 22.8 to 26.1 earlier). Professional rugby is about 75 and would be too high for URBA. One team fields 15 starters x 80 min = 20 player-hours per match (about 21 with replacements), so about 0.6-0.65 new injuries per club per match and about 16-17 per club per 26-match season. Spread over a 40+ player senior squad this keeps simultaneous absentees around 3-6, not half the squad. Training: 2 per 1000 training hours is a game-tuning value (unverified in this session): the Argentine study reports a much lower 0.77, while a post-lockdown URBA Segunda club reports 4.2; treat 0.8-4 as the plausible range. Use 24-36 for match incidence as a difficulty slider.

riskFactors.effect: About 48% of community injuries in 2017-18 and about 61% in 2019-20 happen in the tackle; also the largest share in professionals.
Professional match incidence (75/1000h) is about 2.5x community (29/1000h); injuries last longer on artificial turf (about +6 days mean in PRISP 2021-22).

Not verified this session. Literature pattern (estimate): similar overall rates; backs have more hamstring and calf injuries (use a 1.4-1.6x multiplier on backs, expressed as forwardsBias 0.6), forwards more neck, back and shoulder injuries.
Not verified this session. A prior injury of the same type is a well-established risk factor (reported roughly 1.5-2x for hamstring); suggested game multiplier 1.5 for 8 weeks after return.
Not verified this session. Injury rates are typically higher in the second half and the last quarter; suggested game multiplier about 1.3 after minute 60.

notes: Verified this session from search summaries or abstracts: 75/1000h PRISP 2021-22, mean 44 and median 18 days; CRISP 29.2, 26.1 and 22.8; concussion 17% community and 24% professional; Argentine 30.9 match and 0.77 training; knee 38% of days lost, head and face 15%, shoulder 14%.

Not verified: the full report PDFs (keepyourbootson.co.uk certificate expired, PMC and englandrugby.com blocked scraping), so per-type shares for non-concussion injuries, per-type days and risk-factor effect sizes are literature-based estimates and are labelled as such. Please re-check against the PDFs before treating them as cited.

Definitions differ: CRISP counts injuries with at least 7 days of absence; PRISP counts at least 1 day (professionals). The Argentine definition should be confirmed in the Tondelli paper. The 30/1000h recommendation assumes a 7-day threshold, so minor knocks should not be simulated as injuries.

Suggested game use: per match roll each player on the field with probability incidence/1000 x minutes/60, pick the type by share (weighted by position bias), then draw days from a skewed distribution near the median within min-max. Cap simultaneous injured players per club (about 8 percent of the squad).
Percentages sum to 1.00 including 'otras'. Days are time-loss to return to play, not to return to selection.
